note: Curated landing sites. Planetocentric lat/lon in degrees, longitude east-positive (-180..180). coord_quality: 'landed' = published landing coordinate (rounded); 'approximate' = region centre or target area, check against the source before relying on it.

sites.name: Lunar South Pole
sites.notes: Geographic pole. The Sun never rises more than about 1.6 deg above a flat horizon here.

sites.name: Shackleton-de Gerlache connecting ridge
sites.notes: One of the best-lit places near the pole (Bussey et al. 2010, Mazarico et al. 2011).

sites.name: Shackleton crater rim
sites.notes: High rim next to a permanently shadowed crater floor.

sites.name: Haworth (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.notes: One of nine candidate regions announced in October 2024.

sites.name: Malapert Massif (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.notes: Massif with long Earth visibility; one of nine regions (Oct 2024).

sites.name: Mons Mouton (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.notes: Flat-topped massif; one of nine regions (Oct 2024).

sites.name: Nobile Rim (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.notes: Rim of Nobile crater; Nobile Rim 1 and 2 are two of nine regions (Oct 2024).

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.notes: Rim of de Gerlache crater; one of nine regions (Oct 2024).

sites.name: Slater Plain (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.notes: One of nine regions (Oct 2024).

sites.name: Peak near Cabeus B (Artemis III candidate region)
sites.notes: One of nine regions (Oct 2024).

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (Malapert A area)
sites.notes: Landed 22 Feb 2024, tipped on its side.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton)
sites.notes: Landed 6 Mar 2025 in a crater near the target, on its side.

sites.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Mare Crisium)
sites.notes: Landed 2 Mar 2025 near Mons Latreille, full mission completed.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (Shiv Shakti point)
sites.notes: Landed 23 Aug 2023, southernmost soft landing at the time.

sites.name: SLIM (Shioli crater)
sites.notes: Pinpoint landing 19 Jan 2024, landed upside down; solar panels faced west.

sites.name: Chang'e 3 (Mare Imbrium)
sites.notes: Landed 14 Dec 2013 with the Yutu rover.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 (Von Karman crater, far side)
sites.notes: First far-side landing, 3 Jan 2019. Earth is never visible: needs the Queqiao relay.

sites.name: Chang'e 5 (Mons Rumker)
sites.notes: Sample return, landed 1 Dec 2020.

sites.name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo basin, far side)
sites.notes: First far-side sample return, landed 1 Jun 2024. No direct Earth link.

sites.name: Luna 9 (Oceanus Procellarum)
sites.notes: First soft landing, 3 Feb 1966.

sites.name: Apollo 12 (Oceanus Procellarum)
sites.notes: 19 Nov 1969, next to Surveyor 3.
